newsitem.title: CHINA: Ogilvy & Mather sees 1997 China revenue doubling.
newsitem.headline: Ogilvy & Mather sees 1997 China revenue doubling.

text.p: Ogilvy & Mather Advertising Ltd expects revenue from its three branches in China to double in 1997 to around 800 million yuan from 400 million yuan in 1996, a company official said on Tuesday.
Shelly Lazarus, Ogilvy & Mather's chief executive officer, told a business conference that China's market was developing fast.
She said Ogilvy & Mather wanted to help Chinese companies build brandnames rather than just sell products.
The U.S. company, one of biggest advertising firms in China, has branches in Beijing, Shanghai and Guangzhou. It opened its first office in the country in 1991.
